newsitem.title: ITALY: Ciampi says optimistic over Italy EMU entry.
newsitem.headline: Ciampi says optimistic over Italy EMU entry.

text.p: Italy is already in line with two of three of the Maastricht criteria, on inflation and interest rates, and with the one-off "Euro tax" will soon have the deficit/GDP ratio on course, Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi was quoted as saying.

"Six months ago we were outside all three main Maastricht parameters, but we rolled our sleeves up and now - on inflation and rates - we are in line with European requirements," he said in an interview in the daily Corriere della Sera.
"Certainly there is still work to do on the deficit. Did anyone expect us to perform miracles in just a few months?," he said.
He said that since the goverment of Prime Minister Romano Prodi took the decision to toughen up the 1997 budget, "the financial markets' support for our economy came flooding in."
The 62.5 trillion lire austerity budget is due to go before the full lower chamber of deputies for debate on Wednesday and complete its passage there by mid-November.

Ciampi noted that the spread between Italian and German 10-year bonds, "the real indicator of the credit which we enjoy abroad", was at 320 basis points in July before narrowing rapidly to around 220 bps now.
The Bank of Italy last week cut its key discount rate to 7.50 percent from 8.25 percent. Ciampi said at the time this was a just reward for the government's policy of economic rigour.

He said the weight of the extra budgetary measures had been carefully worked out to reduce the impact on the economy. Some 12.5 trillion lire in the 1997 budget is due to come from as yet unspecified Treasury operations, and another 12.5 trillion from a one-off so-called Tax for Europe on incomes.
"It is not tax for a Europe but rather a one-off contribution based on incomes," Ciampi said.
"It will not be necessary to repeat it. The 1997 one-off measure is meant just to bring forward by one year the deficit/GDP goal of 3.0 percent," he said.
As for inflation, Ciampi said that "when last June with (average) inflation still at 4.5 percent we set a goal of 2.5 percent for 1997 we were criticised as if we'd set an impossible target.
"But today, inflation is down to three percent and we will end this year with between 2.7 and 2.8 percent, making possible an average inflation rate of 2.5 percent in 1997," he said.
Ciampi said in a newspaper interview on Friday that Italy aimed to seek re-entry to the exchange rate mechanism (ERM) after the budget has cleared the lower house of parliament.
Italy needs to get the lira back in the erm by year-end in order to have a chance of qualifying for EMU.
"I entered the Prodi government for one reason, for one spewcific duty - to take Italy into Europe (monetary union)," Ciampi told the financial daily Il Sole 24 Ore.
